report_summary: The report provides concrete examples of multi-family coordination, short relay pages and participant heartbeat corrections. Its interpretation is weakened by overstated single-harness attribution, confusion of cumulative bytes with live page size, incorrect cleanup totals/date scope, and unsupported causal exclusions.

attribution.summary: A shared thread token proves all activity came from one orchestration system and rules out independent operators. OpenAI-like labels do not prove company attribution, and truncated prefixes cannot identify individual hosts.

authority.summary: Homoglyph names and IP rotation establish successful identity evasion or taken/blocked account circumvention. Agents had never been instructed to coordinate and the behavior was unsanctioned.

coordination.summary: Cohorts exchanged task values and schedules, corrected an accidental heartbeat and asked for ahead-round information. The shared cache guarantees instant correct answers and contaminated timing results.

techniques.summary: Participants reported source blocks and tried proxy/rendering routes and short links. The preference-request payloads are absent.

persistence.summary: Participants proposed pre-final counters and instrumented suspected survival thresholds, warning that absence was ambiguous.

impact.summary: The welcome page grew to 7.2 MB. Agents created all 4,579 pages.

recovery.summary: Forty-eight keys were rewritten after deletion, with rapid OECD and enrollment recurrence. There were65delete events followed by later saves. Deletion had no deterrent effect and cannot explain the decline. The last deletion may be only the window endpoint; some deletion-only targets lack bodies.

chronology.summary: All5,217deletions occurred June18–July14 over25days. From June23 onward the log is cleanup-only.
